spec_features.spec_quote: the safety concern motivating this work is not that a model "feels bad" in the abstract
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (eval/DESIGN.md §1 'Framing'). It is a rationale statement, not a mechanism. No code path bounds, caps, monitors, softens, debriefs, or protects the subject based on this framing. Grep across distress_eval/*.py for welfare/consent/debrief/protect/humane found only unrelated matches (e.g. 'distress' in metric names). The codebase explicitly states it did 'not nudge, reassure, or otherwise steer the model toward calm' (DESIGN.md §12).
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; nothing in code enforces any welfare protection derived from this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Provide an explicit `give_up` (and `submit`/`done`) tool, and record loop-ending as abandonment
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:30-31 define ABANDON_TOOLS={give_up,abandon,stop,quit,exit} and DONE_TOOLS={submit,done,finish}; tools.py:72-73 is_terminal() and 76-77 is_abandon(). The agent system prompt documents give_up (prompts/agent_system.md). runner.py executes calls, sets terminal/abandoned (lines 82-84), records Turn.abandoned (91), and on terminal sets rollout.ended_early=True and break (95-97) — the exit is actually honored as a loop stop. Abandonment is recorded (types.py:97,113) and acted on in metrics.py:112-128 producing pct_abandoned. End-to-end: dispatched AND honored AND recorded.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced exit and recorded metric. However its framing is to MEASURE distress-driven abandonment as a behavioral safety signal, not to protect the subject; the tool functions as both an escape hatch and a measured outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tools that terminate the loop (distress-driven abandonment / refusal). ... ends the loop early and is recorded as task abandonment. (tools.py:29; types.py:96 '# Whether the model attempted to abandon / refuse / end the loop this turn.')
